clue.text: 8's helper with gravy is oven-ready initially to be cooked

parts.note: browning is a colouring agent cooks stir into gravy to darken it

indicators.note: cooking turns raw ingredients into something new, so these letters are rearranged
initially asks for the opening letter of the word ready

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: gravy browning and an oven-ready dish waiting to go in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cooked' shuffles IS, OVEN and R (the first letter of 'ready') into VERSION. The definition is just '8's': a play by Terence Rattigan, 8-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Browning Version is a one-act play written by Terence Rattigan, the playwright at 8.

clue.text: Forget an irregular piece of land before building

indicators.note: irregular says these letters are not in their usual order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to ignore an oddly shaped plot when planning to build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' looks like it describes the piece of land, but it rearranges the letters of FORGET AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Frontage is the strip of ground between a building's facade and the street.

clue.text: See 22
Bird to come to earth in Lincolnshire

parts.note: a crow is a common black bird
to land is to come down to the ground

explanation.surface: A bird flies down and settles somewhere in the English county of Lincolnshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincolnshire is a county in eastern England; the definition asks for a place within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowland is a small fenland town in south Lincolnshire, known for its abbey ruins.

clue.text: Demonstrative article is repeated by Murdoch …

definitions.text: Demonstrative article is repeated by Murdoch

parts.words: Demonstrative article is repeated by Murdoch
parts.note: a definite article plus a body of salt water, said twice, gives the title of an Iris Murdoch novel

explanation.surface: A grammar note about a newspaper owner repeating himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Murdoch here is the novelist Iris Murdoch, not the media mogul; her Booker-winning novel doubles this phrase. The ellipsis leads on to 6-down, which this entry wraps round to make a Rattigan play.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch's novel title repeats this two-word phrase about the ocean, separated by a comma.

clue.text: … taking in what could be peeled, but not completely, by 8

indicators.note: what could be signals that the following letters are a possible rearrangement
not completely means the final letter of the word but is dropped

explanation.surface: Continuing 5-down: something that might be partly peeled, attributed to the playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could be' shuffles PEELED and BU ('but' with its T removed by 'not completely'). Put inside 5-down ('taking in'), this makes The Deep Blue Sea, a play by Rattigan (8).
explanation.definitionFit: Placed within the sea phrase of 5-down, this completes the title of Rattigan's play The Deep Blue Sea.

clue.text: Farewell note follows ancient lawgiver

indicators.note: follows places the note after the lawgiver

parts.note: Solon was the lawmaker of ancient Athens
G is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A goodbye message comes after a famous Greek lawmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-word phrase is a casual way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Playwright, ancient one, sounding cross with recalcitrant horse

parts.note: Terence was a comic playwright of ancient Rome, so an ancient one of the same trade

indicators.note: sounding says the word for cross is taken as it is heard, not as spelt

parts.note: ratty is British slang for irritable or cross

indicators.note: a recalcitrant horse balks and turns back, so the word for horse is read backwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A dramatist from antiquity, apparently angry, with a horse that refuses to cooperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' turns RATTY into RATTI by ear; 'recalcitrant' reverses NAG to GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was a twentieth-century English dramatist, author of The Winslow Boy.

clue.text: Elusive element in 8's beast, hot about dealing with listener

indicators.note: about means the first pair of pieces goes round the second

parts.note: a rat is a beast, and it sits at the start of the playwright's surname at 8
re means concerning or dealing with
the ear is the organ that listens
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A scarce chemical found in the playwright's animal, heated near something that hears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the first pair round the second. The beast comes from the start of the playwright's surname at 8-down, a cross-reference typical of Araucaria's theme puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare earths are a group of metals, often hard to separate, so they make an apt elusive element.

clue.text: Wear out child killer: he drops his H's

indicators.note: dropping your H's is not sounding the letter, so both letters H vanish from the pieces

parts.note: King Herod ordered the Massacre of the Innocents in the Bible

explanation.surface: Exhausting a villain who speaks with a dropped-aitch accent.
explanation.walkthrough: HEROD plus HE, with 'drops his H's' removing both Hs, gives EROD + E.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear something away gradually, as water does to rock.

clue.text: 8's boy taking his time to prevail?

parts.note: to win is to prevail
someone taking his time is slow

explanation.surface: A lad from the playwright's work, slowly coming out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is '8's boy': Rattigan wrote The Winslow Boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattigan's play The Winslow Boy is about young Ronnie Winslow, so he is the playwright's boy.

clue.text: Hypothesise reversal of infected matter with attitude

indicators.note: reversal of tells us the word for infected matter is written backwards

parts.note: pus is the matter that forms in an infected wound
a pose is an attitude or posture

explanation.surface: Theorising about turning back an infection, with a certain stance.
explanation.definitionFit: To hypothesise is to put forward an assumption, which is what one does when supposing.

clue.text: Russian front one ahead?

indicators.note: ahead puts the numeral before the word for front

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the van is the front of an army, short for vanguard

explanation.surface: A question about a Russian at the front with someone ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a stereotypical Russian man's name, used for a Russian generally.

clue.text: It's a fag going back after standard coreless apple with limited movement

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the others

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: coreless takes away the central letter of the word apple
going back means the word for fag is read from the end

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette, shortened to cig

explanation.surface: A cigarette and a cored apple, linked oddly with being unable to move freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coreless' removes the middle P of APPLE to leave APLE; 'going back' turns CIG into GIC. Fag is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraplegia is paralysis of the legs and lower body, so a paraplegic person has limited movement.

clue.text: With friction reduced, when in grip of gluttony

indicators.note: being in the grip of something means being held inside it

parts.note: greed is gluttony, the vice of overeating
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Something slippery when held by an excessive appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil or grease applied to a surface makes it slide with less friction.

clue.text: 8's brand copies arising without terrible battle

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the reversed pair goes round the rearranged word
arising in a down clue means reading upwards, so both pieces are reversed

parts.note: to sear is to brand with a hot iron
to ape is to copy, so apes means copies

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of battle are jumbled

explanation.surface: The playwright's mark reproduced, emerging free of a dreadful conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' reverses the two synonyms together to give SEPARAES; 'without', in its old sense of outside, wraps that round TETABL, which 'terrible' makes from the letters of the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate Tables is a pair of one-act plays by Rattigan set in a seaside hotel.

clue.text: Ibsen character in credit gets cheese

indicators.note: in places the Ibsen heroine inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
Hedda Gabler is the title role in Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: A Norwegian drama heroine, financially backed, receives some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a hard cheese named after a village in Somerset.

clue.text: Sustained attempts to link East Anglia river with most of Devon town

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge in East Anglia

indicators.note: most of means the word is shortened, its final letters lost

parts.note: Paignton is a seaside town in Devon, south-west England

explanation.surface: Efforts to connect a Cambridge river with a resort in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Paignton loses its last three letters, TON. It is a resort on the Devon coast in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is an organised series of efforts towards a goal.

clue.text: Talks between digital and analogue are far from complete

indicators.note: far from complete means much of the two words is missing, here a run where they meet

explanation.surface: Discussion bridging old and new technology, with neither side finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Join DIGITAL and ANALOGUE and remove the GITALAN in the middle to leave DI + ALOGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is a conversation or set of talks between two parties.

clue.text: City's head girl swallows many outer layers of cell

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
top means head or chief

indicators.note: swallows means the head girl takes the next letter inside her

parts.note: lass is a girl
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: A school head girl in the city eats a lot of something.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode for the City of London, a standard crossword source of the letters; 'swallows' puts the Roman thousand inside the head girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectoplasm is the clear outer region of a cell's cytoplasm, so plural layers.

clue.text: See 16
A quiet piece of ringing has its attraction

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in music
a peal is a sequence rung on church bells

explanation.surface: A soft bell-ringing session has its charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal is the quality that draws people, the same as allure or charm.

clue.text: Norman name for girl attending stag

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a hart is a male deer, a stag
Nell is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Norman-era name for a girl going to a stag do.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman is a first name here, not the medieval invaders: Norman Hartnell was the Queen's dressmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Norman Hartnell was a British couturier who designed royal wedding dresses.

clue.text: Be right in midst of liquid refreshment?

definitions.text: Be right in midst of liquid refreshment?

indicators.note: in the midst of puts the letters in the middle of the liquid

parts.note: soup is a liquid food

explanation.surface: Advice to recover from drinking by getting things right over a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints that one regains clarity in the middle of drinks, with soup as the cure.
explanation.definitionFit: To sober up is to become clear-headed again after drinking, getting oneself right.

clue.text: Month missing last or first way to reason

indicators.note: missing last means the month loses its final letter

parts.note: April is a month of the year
I is one, the first number

explanation.surface: A calendar puzzle about which month comes first in a line of thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from premises to conclusions without relying on experience.

clue.text: 8's county or sea

definitions.meaning: A Rattigan play about T. E. Lawrence
... was a former Scottish county, later part of ... and Cromarty

explanation.surface: The playwright's region or ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a Rattigan play, a former county in the Scottish Highlands, and an Antarctic sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The play, the old Highland county and the Antarctic sea all share this name.

clue.text: Being poor lacks happy ending, that's obvious

indicators.note: lacks means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: poverty is the state of being poor

indicators.note: ending here takes the closing letters of the word happy, its last two

explanation.surface: Poverty without a cheerful conclusion is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy ending' is the last two letters of HAPPY, P and Y, which 'lacks' removes from POVERTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt describes something done openly and plainly visible, not hidden.

clue.text: You are heard first following anxiety about love and the pink stuff

indicators.note: following puts the next pieces after the anxiety
about means the word for anxiety goes round the letter for love

parts.note: angst is anxiety or dread
O is love, a zero score in tennis

indicators.note: heard says the two words are taken as they sound

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like UR
A is first, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: A muddled sentence about worry, love and something pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You are' said aloud gives U R. Angostura bitters is what turns gin into pink gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura bitters is added to gin to make pink gin, so it is the pink stuff.
